claims.statement: Fork-triggered workflows do not receive secrets except GITHUB_TOKEN; parent event/private-fork settings must be resolved rather than extending this reusable into every possible privileged event.

Fork permissions can add/remove read access but usually cannot grant writes; an administrator's Send write tokens to workflows from pull requests setting is the described exception, not a safe default or authorization to enable it.
Actions Importer authentication uses environment variables populated through configure; reviewing this reference does not run configuration or acquire credentials.
Custom transformers may handle unknown steps or partially successful conversions; automatic conversion gaps remain explicit and require review rather than assumed completion.

Importer audit_summary reports pipeline conversion statistics: Successful means all constructs/items automatically converted, Partially successful all constructs but some items unconverted, Unsupported definition type, Failed fatal conversion from invalid source, internal error or inaccessible network often invalid credentials. Conversion percentage is not verified runtime equivalence.

Build-step audit distinguishes automatically converted known steps, unconverted unknown steps and unsupported/incompatible steps. Action inventory supports GHES synchronization and security allow-list review, not approval to trust every converted action.

Manual tasks identify secrets to create and referenced non-hosted runner labels to provision; these tasks are not completed by successful conversion and require separate credentials/provisioning authority.

Audit manifests include original pipeline, conversion network responses, converted workflow and stack traces; workflow_usage.csv lists actions/secrets/runners only for successfully converted pipelines. These potentially sensitive files require private handling and do not exhaust failed-pipeline inventory.

Successful migrate output links a new workflow PR; inspect Manual steps and Files changed before merging. PR creation, required secret tasks and review are distinct from actual migration completion or merge authorization.
Importer subcommands accept optional arguments to customize migration; this fragment does not define options or authorize execution.
General security-hardening fragment links secure-use guidance; link presence is not a completed review of that page or actual hardened workflow.
GHES Actions is not enabled by default; this is consistent with repository defaults applying only after instance activation, not evidence of current instance state.

Action lookup tries the local instance first, then dotcom only if local repository absent and automatic dotcom access enabled. Matching local repository therefore affects provenance; fallback is conditional, not guaranteed.
Whole github context contains sensitive github.token. Console masking does not make exporting/printing context safe; no real context or token collected.
Inspect currently processed hosted jobs in organization/enterprise to diagnose concurrency and queue constraints; linked procedure and actual counts are separately pending.

FPT organization/repository navigation uses Settings > Actions > Runners; GHEC adds enterprise navigation through Your enterprises and Policies > Actions > Runners tab. UI route is not authorization or evidence of accessible data.
GitHub-hosted runners table entry appears only when using those runners; absent entry is not universal proof of no runner configuration or permission availability.

GITHUB_TOKEN permissions support read/write/none for actions, checks, contents, deployments, issues, discussions, packages, pages, pull-requests, security-events and statuses; artifact-metadata, attestations and code-quality are feature-conditional. FPT/GHEC id-token supports write/none; conditional vulnerability-alerts supports read/none, not write.

Specifying any individual permission sets unspecified permissions to none. read-all/write-all are aggregate shorthands, and permissions: {} disables all available permissions. Examples are source syntax, not deployed grants.
GITHUB_TOKEN expires at job finish or after at most 24 hours; token presence does not prove freshness or permission sufficiency.

Each job begins with a repository token; this fragment recommends contents: read and packages: write for its enclosing use case. Do not adopt package write for every workflow without parent applicability.
Permission write includes read where supported and unspecified permissions become none. actions: write can cancel runs, which is operational mutation, not mere observation.

Conditional artifact-metadata write creates storage records; attestations write generates build attestations; checks write creates checks; conditional code-quality write uploads coverage. Capabilities are distinct from their truth or enforcement.

contents read lists commits and write creates releases; deployments write creates deployments; discussions write closes/deletes discussions. Permission names do not grant actual authority for publication/destructive changes.

FPT/GHEC id-token write fetches OIDC tokens, not cloud authorization by itself; issues write comments, packages write uploads/publishes, pages write requests builds and pull-requests write adds labels. External providers/policy still govern use.

security-events read lists code-scanning alerts and write updates status; it cannot read secret-scanning alerts. Dependabot needs conditional vulnerability-alerts, otherwise separate App/PAT; statuses read lists commit statuses. Missing access must stay unknown, not pass.
Conditional vulnerability-alerts permits read/none only; write invalid. read-all and write-all both include it as read, so aggregate write is not unrestricted write across every scope.
github.triggering_actor may differ on rerun, but reruns use github.actor privileges, not the rerun initiator's privileges. Identity fields must not be substituted when evaluating authorization.
Triggering commit SHA depends on the event; illustrated SHA is a placeholder. Event-specific semantics must be resolved rather than always assuming branch head or PR head.
